definitions.explanation: A lottery or prize draw typically held at shopping streets, department stores, or festivals, where participants draw lots (often by pulling strings, spinning a wheel, or drawing a ball from a box) to win prizes.

examples.japanese: {福引|ふくび}きで{一等|いっとう}が{当|あ}たった。
examples.english: I won first prize in the lucky draw.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物|もの}をすると{福引|ふくび}きの{券|けん}がもらえる。
examples.english: When you shop, you can get a lucky draw ticket.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}の{商店街|しょうてんがい}では{福引|ふくび}き{大会|たいかい}が{開|ひら}かれ、{多|おお}くの{客|きゃく}で{賑|にぎ}わっていた。
examples.english: A lucky draw event was held at the shopping street at year's end, bustling with many customers.

notes:
USAGE:
A traditional form of promotional lottery in Japan. The classic format involves a spinning drum (がらがら) from which colored balls fall out, with each color corresponding to a prize tier.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {福引|ふくび}きを{引|ひ}く (to draw in a lucky draw)
- {福引|ふくび}き{券|けん} (lucky draw ticket)
- {福引|ふくび}き{大会|たいかい} (lucky draw event)
- {福引|ふくび}きで{当|あ}たる (to win in a lucky draw)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Often seen during {年末|ねんまつ} (year-end) sales and {歳末|さいまつ}{大売|おおう}り{出|だ}し (end-of-year sales), and at {縁日|えんにち} (festival days) at shrines and temples.
